issues.description: The template's StockIngredient class exposes the ingredient quantity via a method named retrieveQuantity(), while other template classes (Stock) and the solution expect a method named getQuantity(). This name mismatch causes compilation errors and prevents students from running or completing the exercise (Stock.java calls getQuantity(), which does not exist in the template StockIngredient).
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() in src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java (or add a new getQuantity() delegating to retrieveQuantity()) so method names match Stock.java and other usages. This aligns the template with the solution and the instruction to provide standard getters for private fields.

issues.description: The problem statement requires adding standard getters for private fields (e.g., getQuantity) and the solution implements StockIngredient.getQuantity(), but the template StockIngredient class declares the quantity accessor as retrieveQuantity(). This inconsistent identifier breaks the expected mapping between the specification and the starter code and also causes the template Stock class (which calls getQuantity()) to be out-of-sync with the template StockIngredient API, likely leading to confusion or compile errors for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template accessor retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() (and update any callers), or alternatively change callers in the template to use retrieveQuantity(), so that the template, problem statement expectation, and solution all consistently use getQuantity() for the quantity getter.
